about: The muscles and fibrous layers of the wall of the abdomen and its posterior wall: the rectus and its sheath, the three flat muscles and their aponeuroses, the linea alba, pyramidalis, the inguinal ligament and canal, and psoas, iliacus and quadratus lumborum, drawn on the trunk's own surface and attached to the model's hip bones, ribs, cartilages and lumbar vertebrae. Skeletal muscle: the drives are muscle tone (rigidity and paralysis), a seizure, shivering, vomiting and respiratory drive for the wall muscles of forced expiration, and exertion for the posterior wall. The layers' thicknesses are drawing choices; the cremaster, anal sphincter, perineal muscles and diaphragm belong to other organs. The inguinal canal is schematic and empty.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Rectus Abdominis
parts.summary: The paired straight muscle of the front of the abdomen
parts.function: It runs from the costal cartilages and xiphoid process to the pubis inside its sheath. It flexes the trunk and, with the other wall muscles, forces air out and compresses the abdomen.

drives.note: Vomiting is forced by contraction of the abdominal wall muscles; the engine's vomiting signal is 0 or 1. The weight is a display scale.

Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those recruited when breathing is driven harder (accessory inspiration or forced expiration), so a rise in central respiratory drive engages it. The weight is a display scale.
Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.
Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis, or a neuromuscular blocker) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. The weight is a display scale.
A seizure is a brief, intense motor discharge, which the engine reports as 0 or 1; skeletal muscle contracts in it. The weight is a display scale.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle in the cold, so this muscle is engaged by it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Tendinous Intersections
parts.summary: Fibrous bands across the muscle
parts.function: They divide the rectus into segments and fix it to the front of its sheath. Gray's: usually three.

parts.label: Rectus Sheath
parts.summary: The fibrous case round the rectus
parts.function: It is formed by the aponeuroses of the three flat muscles. It encloses the rectus and its layers differ above and below the arcuate line.

parts.label: Anterior Layer of Rectus Sheath
parts.summary: The layer in front of the muscle
parts.function: It covers the front of the rectus for its whole length.

parts.label: Posterior Layer of Rectus Sheath
parts.summary: The layer behind the muscle
parts.function: It lies behind the rectus down to the arcuate line.

parts.label: Arcuate Line
parts.summary: The lower edge of the posterior layer
parts.function: Below it the aponeuroses pass in front of the rectus, which then lies directly on the transversalis fascia.

parts.label: Linea Alba
parts.summary: The midline band between the two recti
parts.function: Fibres of the three aponeuroses meet here from the xiphoid process to the pubic symphysis.

parts.label: External Oblique
parts.summary: The outermost flat muscle of the flank
parts.function: It runs from the lower ribs down and forward to the iliac crest, the linea alba and the inguinal ligament. It rotates and flexes the trunk, and compresses the abdomen.

parts.label: Muscular Part of External Oblique
parts.summary: The fleshy part of the flank
parts.function: It ends at the lateral border of the rectus, the semilunar line.

parts.label: Aponeurosis of External Oblique
parts.summary: The broad tendon sheet in front of the rectus
parts.function: It carries on to the linea alba and its lower border is rolled under to form the inguinal ligament.

parts.label: Internal Oblique
parts.summary: The middle flat muscle of the flank
parts.function: It runs from the iliac crest and inguinal ligament up and forward to the lower ribs and the rectus sheath, at right angles to the external oblique.

parts.label: Transversus Abdominis
parts.summary: The deepest flat muscle
parts.function: It runs transversely from the lower costal cartilages, the iliac crest and the inguinal ligament to the linea alba and compresses the abdominal contents.

parts.label: Pyramidalis
parts.summary: A small triangular muscle in front of the lower rectus
parts.function: It runs from the pubis to the linea alba and tenses it. It is absent in some people.

parts.label: Inguinal Ligament
parts.summary: The band from the hip bone to the pubis
parts.function: It runs from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle and is the rolled lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis.

parts.label: Inguinal Canal
parts.summary: An oblique channel through the lower wall
parts.function: It passes above the inguinal ligament from the deep ring to the superficial ring. Drawn as a schematic glass channel; nothing passes through it here.

parts.label: Deep Inguinal Ring
parts.summary: The inner opening of the canal
parts.function: It lies in the transversalis fascia about half way along the inguinal ligament.

parts.label: Superficial Inguinal Ring
parts.summary: The outer opening of the canal
parts.function: It is a gap in the external oblique aponeurosis above the pubic crest.

parts.label: Posterior Abdominal Wall
parts.summary: The muscles beside the lumbar spine
parts.function: Psoas, iliacus and quadratus lumborum form the back wall of the abdomen, behind the kidneys.

drives.note: Exercise engages the muscles that move and steady the trunk and hip, so a rise in exertion engages this muscle. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Psoas Major
parts.summary: The long muscle beside the lumbar vertebrae
parts.function: It runs from the sides of the lumbar bodies over the pelvic brim to the lesser trochanter of the femur and flexes the hip.

parts.label: Psoas Minor
parts.summary: A slender muscle in front of the psoas major
parts.function: It runs from the upper lumbar bodies to the pubis. It is not always present.

parts.label: Iliacus
parts.summary: The fan-shaped muscle of the iliac fossa
parts.function: It arises from the inner face of the iliac plate and joins the psoas tendon, flexing the hip.

parts.label: Quadratus Lumborum
parts.summary: The muscle between the twelfth rib and the iliac crest
parts.function: It lies behind the kidney and bends the trunk to the side and fixes the last rib.
